'''Lenox Hill''' ({{IPAc-en|ˌ|l|ɛ|n|ə|k|s|_|ˈ|h|ɪ|l}}) is a neighborhood on the [[Upper East Side]] of [[Manhattan]] in [[New York City]]. It forms the lower (southern) section of the Upper East Side, east of [[Park Avenue]] in the [[List of numbered streets in Manhattan|60s and 70s]].<ref name=LivingIn>{{cite web | last=Bloom | first=Jennifer Kingson | title=If You're Thinking of Living In: Lenox Hill;Fast-Paced, Often Noisy, Young at Heart | website=The New York Times | date=December 31, 1995 | url=https://www.nytimes.com/1995/12/31/realestate/if-you-re-thinking-of-living-in-lenox-hill-fast-paced-often-noisy-young-at-heart.html | access-date=October 27, 2018}}</ref>

A significant portion of the neighborhood lies within the [[Upper East Side Historic District]], designated by the [[New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission]] in 1981 and expanded in 2010.<ref name=aia>{{cite aia5|page=419}}</ref> The neighborhood is part of [[Manhattan Community Board 8]].

==Geography==
Based on the location of the original Lenox Hill, which was on a farm that spanned present-day 68th Street to [[74th Street (Manhattan)|74th Street]], east of [[Fifth Avenue (Manhattan)|Fifth Avenue]], ''[[The Encyclopedia of New York City]]'' defines the neighborhood as the area between 60th Street and 77th Street, from Fifth Avenue on the west to [[Lexington Avenue]] on the east.<ref name="encyclopediany">{{cite encyclopedia|last=Mendelsohn|first=Joyce|editor1-link=Kenneth T. Jackson|editor1-last=Jackson|editor1-first=Kenneth T.|encyclopedia=[[The Encyclopedia of New York City]]|title=Lenox Hill|url=https://archive.org/details/encyclopediaofne0000unse_q5q3/page/732/mode/2up|access-date=July 1, 2023|edition=1st|date=1995|publisher=[[Yale University Press]]|isbn=0300055366|page=732}}</ref>

However, neighborhood boundaries can shift and most residents see the modern boundaries differently, as the [[United States Post Office (Lenox Hill Station)|Lenox Hill post office]] and the neighborhood's service-oriented retail shops are located east of [[Lexington Avenue]].<ref name=LivingIn/><ref name="UES">https://web.archive.org/web/20200322090522/https://www.friends-ues.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/FRIENDS_FINAL-10.01.15.pdf , archived from [https://www.friends-ues.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/FRIENDS_FINAL-10.01.15.pdf]</ref> Many city maps also place Lenox Hill in the lower ''east'' section of the Upper East Side,<ref>[https://www1.nyc.gov/assets/doh/downloads/pdf/epi/Manhattan_Political.pdf Manhattan: City Council, Assembly, and State Senate]{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.baruch.cuny.edu/nycdata/population-geography/maps-boroughdistricts.htm|title=NYCdata: Maps - Boroughs with Community Districts|website=www.baruch.cuny.edu}}</ref> including maps of [[Manhattan Community Board 8|Manhattan Community District 8]],<ref>{{Cite web| title=Partial map of New York City | url=http://photos1.blogger.com/blogger/7514/2288/1600/cb8%20map.jpg | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190405171239/http://photos1.blogger.com/blogger/7514/2288/1600/cb8%20map.jpg | archive-date=2019-04-05}}</ref> the [[New York City Department of City Planning]],<ref>[https://www1.nyc.gov/site/planning/data-maps/city-neighborhoods.page NYC Neighborhoods Map]</ref> the [[New York City Department of Transportation]],<ref>[https://www1.nyc.gov/html/dot/downloads/pdf/yorkville.pdf Yorkville, Manhattan: Senior Pedestrian Crashes 2001-2006]</ref> NYCityMap (by the [[New York City Department of Information Technology and Telecommunications]]),<ref>[http://gis.nyc.gov/doitt/nycitymap/ NYCityMap]. The words "Lenox Hill" appear over the area east of Second Avenue, between 59th Street and 79th Street. Searching "Lenox Hill" centers a star on a block on First Avenue between 69th Street and 70th Street. Accessed May 7, 2021.</ref> and the Friends of the Upper East Side.<ref name=UES/>
{{clear left}}

==History==
The neighborhood is named for the hill that "stood at what became 70th Street and [[Park Avenue (Manhattan)|Park Avenue]]."<ref name=encyclopediany /> The name "Lenox" is that of the Scottish merchant settler [[Robert Lenox]] (1759-1839),<ref>[http://www.nypl.org/research/chss/spe/rbk/faids/lenox.pdf (New York Public Library) ''Guide to the James Lenox Papers'']; James Trager, ''The New York Chronology''. s.v. "1840" [sic].  {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061210222445/http://www.nypl.org/research/chss/spe/rbk/faids/lenox.pdf |date=December 10, 2006 }}</ref> who owned about {{convert|30|acre|m2}} of land "at the five-mile (8 km) stone", reaching from Fifth to Fourth (now Park) Avenues and from East [[74th Street (Manhattan)|74th]] to 68th Streets.<ref name=nytheirs>{{cite news | url = https://timesmachine.nytimes.com/timesmachine/1886/09/14/103980269.pdf | title = Miss Lenox's Heirs | work =[[The New York Times]] | date =14 September 1886 | access-date = February 22, 2013}}</ref> For the sum of $6,420 (${{formatnum:{{Inflation|US|6420|1818|r=-3}}}} in current dollar terms)<ref>Morrison (1906), p. 85f</ref> or $6,920 (${{formatnum:{{Inflation|US|6920|1818|r=-3}}}})<ref name=nytheirs /> he had purchased a first set of three parcels in 1818, at an auction held at the [[Tontine Coffee House]] of mortgaged premises of [[Gracie Mansion|Archibald Gracie]], in order to protect Gracie's heirs from foreclosure, as he was executor of Gracie's estate.<ref name=nytheirs /> Several months later he purchased three further parcels, extending his property north to 74th Street.<ref>Wilson, James Grant. ''The Memorial History of the City of New-York from Its First Settlement...'' 1893, p. 10</ref> According to one source, "Thereafter these two tracts were known as the 'Lenox Farm.'"<ref>Morrison (1906)</ref> The tenant farmhouse stood on the rise of ground between Fifth and Madison avenues and 70th and 71st Streets, which would have been the hill, if the property had ever been called "Lenox Hill." The railroad right-of-way of the [[New York & Harlem Railroad]] passed along the east boundary of the property.

[[File:A history of real estate, building and architecture in New York City during the last quarter of a century (1898) (14587163619).jpg|thumb|Union Theological Seminary on Park Avenue, in Lenox Hill (1883).]]
[[Robert Lenox]]'s son [[James Lenox]] divided most of the farm into blocks of building lots and sold them during the 1860s and 1870s;<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/1918/12/15/archives/realty-romance-in-old-lenox-farm-fifth-avenue-land-sold-by-city-in.html "Realty Romance in Old Lenox Farm"], ''[[The New York Times]]'' (December 15, 1918); the occasion was the auction of the auction sale an 1874 map of the section of Robert Lenox's farm that lay between 71st and 74th Streets.</ref> he also donated land for the [[Union Theological Seminary in the City of New York|Union Theological Seminary]] along the railroad right-of-way, between 69th and 70th Streets, and just north of it a full square block between Madison and Fourth Avenue, 70th and 71st streets, for the Presbyterian Hospital, which occupied seven somewhat austere structures on the plot;<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/1892/07/03/archives/founded-by-james-lenox-this-chief-features-of-the-presbyterian.html "Founded by James Lenox, the chief features of the Presbyterian Hospital...], ''[[The New York Times]]'' (July 3, 1892)</ref> He built the [[Lenox Library (New York)|Lenox Library]] on a full block-front of Fifth Avenue, now the site of the [[Frick Collection]].

==Structures==
[[Lenox Hill Hospital]], the former German Hospital, is located in this area, on East 77th Street.

Luxury residences built in the 1910s and 1920s are now very expensive. [[Park Avenue]] and [[Lexington Avenue]] both pass through Lenox Hill, and along these avenues, there are many [[boutique]]s, [[art gallery|art galleries]] and five-star [[hotel]]s. Museums in the area include the Frick Collection.<ref>{{cite enc-nyc2|page=}}.732</ref>

==Demographics==

Based on data from the [[2010 United States census]], the population of Lenox Hill and [[Roosevelt Island]], which are combined into one census tabulation area, was 80,771, an increase of 4,140 (5.4%) from the 76,631 counted in 2000. Covering an area of {{convert|511.71|acres}}, the neighborhood had a population density of {{convert|157.8|PD/acre|PD/sqmi}}.<ref>[http://www1.nyc.gov/assets/planning/download/pdf/data-maps/nyc-population/census2010/t_pl_p5_nta.pdf Table PL-P5 NTA: Total Population and Persons Per Acre – New York City Neighborhood Tabulation Areas*, 2010], Population Division – New York City Department of City Planning, February 2012. Accessed May 18, 2016.</ref> The median income for a household living in Lenox Hill was $92,219.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.city-data.com/neighborhood/Lenox-Hill-New-York-NY.html|title=Lenox Hill neighborhood in New York, New York (NY)|publisher=city-data.com|access-date=2012-12-22}}</ref>

The racial makeup of the neighborhood was 75.3% (60,831) [[White (U.S. Census)|White]], 4.4% (3,571) [[African American (U.S. Census)|African American]], 0.1% (57) [[Native American (U.S. Census)|Native American]], 10.6% (8,569) [[Asian (U.S. Census)|Asian]], 0.1% (61) [[Pacific Islander (U.S. Census)|Pacific Islander]], 0.3% (262) from [[Race (United States Census)|other races]], and 1.9% (1,558) from two or more races. [[Hispanic (U.S. Census)|Hispanic]] or [[Latino (U.S. Census)|Latino]] of any race was 7.3% (5,862) of the population.<ref>[http://www1.nyc.gov/assets/planning/download/pdf/data-maps/nyc-population/census2010/t_pl_p3a_nta.pdf Table PL-P3A NTA: Total Population by Mutually Exclusive Race and Hispanic Origin – New York City Neighborhood Tabulation Areas*, 2010], Population Division – New York City Department of City Planning, March 29, 2011. Accessed May 18, 2016.</ref>

The racial composition of Lenox Hill / Roosevelt Island changed moderately from 2000 to 2010. The most significant changes were the increase in the Asian population by 38% (2,346) and the increase in the Hispanic / Latino population by 22% (1,064). The White population remained the majority with a slight increase of 1% (360), while the small Black population increased by 2% (61); the even smaller population of all other races increased by 19% (309).<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.urbanresearchmaps.org/plurality/files/RaceEthnic%20Change%20by%20Neighborhood%205-23-11.xls | title = Race / Ethnic Change by Neighborhood | publisher = Center for Urban Research, The Graduate Center, CUNY | date = 23 May 2011 | access-date = March 21, 2020 |format=Excel file}}</ref>

==Notable people==
{{main|List of people from the Upper East Side}}
Residents of Lenox Hill have included:
* [[James Lenox]] (1800–1880), philanthropist, founder of [[Lenox Library (New York City)|Lenox Library]]<ref>Gregoire, Chloe. [https://www.villagepreservation.org/2024/08/19/james-lenox-and-the-new-york-public-librarys-greenwich-village-beginnings/ "James Lenox and the New York Public Library’s Greenwich Village Beginnings"], [[Greenwich Village Society for Historic Preservation]], August 19, 2024. Accessed December 26, 2024. "When Robert died in 1839, James inherited the family business, and 300 acres of property on today’s Upper East Side, comprising what is now known as Lenox Hill."</ref>
* [[Robert Lenox]] (1759–1839), merchant, namesake of Lenox Hill<ref>Cohen, Joyce. [https://www.nytimes.com/2002/07/28/realestate/if-you-re-thinking-living-lenox-hill-other-east-side-livelier-less-plush.html "If You're Thinking of Living In/Lenox Hill; 'The Other East Side': Livelier, Less Plush"], ''[[The New York Times]]'', July 28, 2002. Accessed December 26, 2024. "The neighborhood Lenox Hill is actually east of its namesake hill, which took its name from the 30-acre farm of the Scotsman Robert Lenox who died in 1840. His farm occupied what is now 68th to 74th Streets between Park and Fifth Avenues."</ref>
* [[Andy Warhol]] (1928–1987), artist<ref>[https://therealdeal.com/new-york/2019/01/24/lenox-hill-townhouse-where-andy-warhol-partied-sells-for-18m/ "Lenox Hill townhouse where Andy Warhol partied sells for $18M"], ''[[The Real Deal (magazine)|The Real Deal]]'', January 21, 2019. Accessed December 26, 2024.</ref>

==Transportation==
Lenox Hill is serviced by three [[New York City Subway]] stations. These are the [[68th Street–Hunter College station]] on the {{NYCS trains|Lexington local day}}; the [[77th Street station (IRT Lexington Avenue Line)|77th Street station]] on the {{NYCS trains|Lexington local day}}, and the [[72nd Street station (Second Avenue Subway)|72nd Street station]] on the {{NYCS trains|Second}}; and the [[Lexington Avenue–63rd Street station]] on the [[Q (New York City Subway service)|Q]], {{NYCS trains|63rd}}.<ref>{{NYCS const|map}}</ref> Bus routes include {{NYC bus link|M1|M2|M3|M4|M15|M15 SBS|M31|M66|M72|M98|M101|M102|M103}}.<ref>{{Cite NYC bus map|M}}</ref>
